ing: or half orange juice and half lime juice
st: Mix the pork with [[0.5 cup]] sour orange juice, the garlic, onion, [[1 tbsp]] thyme, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper. Marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Put the pork and marinade in a heavy pot with [[1 cup]] water and the whole pepper. Do not cut the pepper open unless you want heat.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 1 hour until the pork is tender and the liquid has mostly cooked off.
Remove the pepper and lift the pork out onto a tray. Pat dry.
Heat [[3 cup]] oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pork in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep brown and crisp outside.
Drain on paper towels. Check that it is above 145°F (63°C).
Serve hot with pikliz and fried plantains.
Season the beef with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and toss with [[2 tbsp]] lime juice. Let sit 15 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot and brown the beef for 8 minutes. Add the onion and garlic and cook 3 minutes.
Add [[10 cup]] water and bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 1 hour until the beef starts to soften.
Boil the squash in a separate pot with a little water for 20 minutes until soft. Blend until smooth and stir the purée into the beef pot.
Add the carrots, potatoes, turnip, celery, cabbage, thyme and the whole pepper. Simmer 25 minutes.
Stir in [[1 cup]] pasta and cook 10 minutes until tender.
Season with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper, remove the pepper and thyme sprigs, and serve hot.
Simmer [[1 cup]] dried mushrooms in [[5 cup]] water for 20 minutes until the water turns inky black.
Strain through a fine sieve, press the mushrooms to extract liquid, and discard them. Keep [[4 cup]] of the black liquid.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil and [[2 tbsp]] butter in a pot. Cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the peas, thyme and whole pepper and stir for 1 minute.
Stir in the rinsed [[2 cup]] rice to coat, then pour in the black liquid and [[1.5 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil, cover, and cook on very low heat for 20 minutes until the rice has absorbed all the liquid.
Rest, covered, for 10 minutes. Remove the pepper and thyme, fluff, and serve.
Put the soaked beans in a pot with [[6 cup]] fresh water and boil hard for 10 minutes, then simmer 50 minutes until completely tender. Kidney beans must be fully cooked.
Drain the beans, saving all of the cooking water.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pot and cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the beans, thyme and whole pepper and stir 2 minutes.
Measure [[3 cup]] of bean water plus [[1 cup]] coconut milk and pour in with [[1.5 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil, add [[2 cup]] rice, stir once, cover, and cook on low for 20 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes, remove the pepper and thyme, fluff and serve.
Combine the cabbage, carrots, onion and peppers in a large bowl.
Add [[2 tsp]] salt and toss.
Pack the mixture into a clean glass jar with the cloves and [[1 tsp]] peppercorns.
Pour in [[1.5 cup]] vinegar and [[0.25 cup]] lime juice until covered.
Close the jar and shake gently.
Refrigerate at least 24 hours before eating, longer for more heat.
Keeps in the fridge for about 2 weeks.
Cut the ends off the plantains, score the peel lengthwise, and peel. Slice into 1 inch rounds.
Heat [[2 cup]] oil in a deep skillet to 325°F (160°C).
Fry the rounds for 3 minutes per side until pale golden and soft inside.
Lift out and place between two sheets of parchment. Press each one flat with the bottom of a jar or a plantain press.
Dip the flattened pieces in salted water (use [[1 tsp]] salt in [[1 cup]] warm water) and pat dry.
Raise the oil to 375°F (190°C) and fry again for 2 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with extra salt. Serve hot.
Season the beef with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large pot and brown the beef for 8 minutes.
Add the onion and garlic and cook 3 minutes, then stir in [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add [[5 cup]] water, thyme and the whole pepper. Cover and simmer for 1 hour until tender.
Add the carrots, chayote, eggplant and cabbage and simmer 25 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, 3 minutes.
Remove the pepper and thyme. Mash the vegetables into the broth with a potato masher until thick and chunky.
Season with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and simmer 5 more minutes. Serve over rice.

ing: peeled and finely grated, or taro
seeded and minced, or to taste
st: Squeeze the grated malanga in a clean towel to remove extra liquid.
Mix it with the garlic, minced pepper, [[2 tbsp]] parsley, scallions, [[2 tbsp]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] black pepper.
Heat [[2 cup]] oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Drop in heaped tablespoons of the mix, 5 or 6 at a time.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Drain the fritters on paper towels to remove extra oil.
Serve hot, with pikliz on the side.

ing: bone-in, cut into 2 inch pieces, or use lamb shoulder
or half orange and half lime juice
st: Rub the goat with the juice, garlic, onion, thyme, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper. Marinate 2 hours or overnight in the fridge.
Place the meat, marinade, whole pepper and [[3 cup]] water in a heavy pot and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours until the meat is very tender. Add water if it runs dry.
Take out the meat, drain well and pat dry. Boil the leftover liquid down to a thick sauce if you like.
Heat [[3 cup]] oil to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the goat in batches for 4 minutes until browned and crisp.
Drain and serve hot with pikliz.

ing: melted, plus extra for the pan
st: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and butter an 8 inch square baking dish.
Mix the sweet potatoes with the banana and [[1 cup]] coconut milk.
Stir in [[0.75 cup]] sugar, [[0.5 cup]] flour, [[3 tbsp]] melted butter, [[1 tsp]] cinnamon, [[0.5 tsp]] nutmeg, [[1 tsp]] vanilla and [[0.25 tsp]] salt.
Spread into the dish and smooth the top.
Bake 60 to 70 minutes until set and the edges are dark brown.
Cool at least 20 minutes, since it firms up as it cools.
Cut into squares and serve warm or cold.
